subject.title: [Bug]: Sandbox container exits immediately when no-new-privileges is applied (exec /usr/bin/sleep: operation not permitted)

question: Should OpenClaw support an operator-visible Docker sandbox recovery path for hosts where `--security-opt no-new-privileges` prevents even `/usr/bin/sleep` from execing?
rationale: The bug is well isolated, but disabling or falling back from `no-new-privileges` changes the Docker sandbox boundary, and repository policy requires explicit operator-controlled security tradeoffs rather than silent compatibility fallback.

options.title: Add explicit dangerous opt-out
options.body: Keep the secure default, add a clearly named `sandbox.docker` opt-out with dangerous-config reporting, docs, focused tests, and real Docker proof for the incompatible-host case.

options.title: Improve diagnostics only
options.body: Keep the hardening unconditional and surface a precise startup/session/doctor error for this EPERM mode without weakening the sandbox.

options.title: Document unsupported host stance
options.body: Treat Docker hosts that reject `no-new-privileges` as unsupported for Docker sandbox mode and direct users to host repair or another sandbox backend.

recommendation.title: Add explicit dangerous opt-out
recommendation.body: Keep the secure default, add a clearly named `sandbox.docker` opt-out with dangerous-config reporting, docs, focused tests, and real Docker proof for the incompatible-host case.

likelyOwner.reason: `steipete` has the strongest recent history on the Docker sandbox dangerous-override and security-policy surfaces this decision would extend.
